# Early Lease Exit Checklist for a London Tenant

A practical review for a tenant ending a lease early in London. This stays general and non-legal-advice, focused on the documents and questions most likely to matter.

## Key Points to Review Before Sending Anything

- **Lease end date and break rights**: Check whether the tenancy agreement has a break clause, notice period, and any conditions for using it.
- **Notice timing**: The landlord was notified on **2026-01-20** for a requested move-out date of **2026-03-15**; confirm whether that matches the notice rule in the agreement.
- **Deposit protection**: A **5-week deposit** usually means the deposit should be protected in an approved scheme; keep the scheme details and certificate handy.
- **Early termination costs**: Review whether the agreement mentions re-letting fees, rent until a replacement tenant is found, or a fixed early-exit charge.
- **Condition and inventory**: Compare the move-in inventory, check-in photos, and any recent inspection notes to reduce disputes over deductions.
- **Utility and council tax handover**: Plan final meter readings, account closures, and the date responsibility ends.
- **Written confirmation**: Aim to get the landlord’s agreement in writing on the move-out date, handover steps, and deposit process.

## Documents to Gather

- Tenancy agreement, including any addendum or renewal document
- The landlord’s or agent’s written notice terms, if separate from the agreement
- Proof of the landlord notification sent on **2026-01-20**
- Deposit protection certificate and scheme details
- Move-in inventory and check-in report
- Any check-out guidance or inspection checklist
- Rent payment history and latest rent statement
- Copies of emails or messages about early termination
- Photos/videos of the property condition, with dates if available
- Final utility meter readings and account references
- Council tax, broadband, and other account closure records if relevant

## Careful Email Template for Early Termination and Deposit Return

Subject: Request to Confirm Early Termination Arrangements and Deposit Return

Dear [Landlord/Agent Name],

I hope you are well. I am writing to confirm the arrangements for my planned move-out from the property at [property address].

As noted in my previous message, I informed you on **2026-01-20** that I intend to leave on **2026-03-15**. Please could you confirm:

- whether this move-out date is accepted;
- any steps required to complete the early termination process;
- whether any fees, rent, or other charges are expected up to the move-out date;
- the process for check-out, handover of keys, and final meter readings; and
- how the deposit return will be handled after the tenancy ends.

I would also appreciate confirmation of the deposit protection scheme details and the next steps for any inspection or check-out report.

I will continue to look after the property and would be grateful for any instructions you would like me to follow before departure.

Thank you for your help. I look forward to your confirmation.

Kind regards,
[Your full name]
[Property address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Review tenancy] https://www.gov.uk/private-renting-tenancy-agreements
Action: [Button: Deposit scheme info] https://www.gov.uk/tenancy-deposit-protection
Action: [Button: Tenant advice] https://england.shelter.org.uk/housing_advice/private_renting

- UK tenancy agreements and private renting guidance: https://www.gov.uk/private-renting-tenancy-agreements
- Tenancy deposit protection: https://www.gov.uk/tenancy-deposit-protection
- Shelter England private renting advice: https://england.shelter.org.uk/housing_advice/private_renting
